html:
SMTO-CFG-0027 — SMTO couldn't apply your permission choice here

GUID: 809cee16-d298-4808-87ae-8f38d426525d
Slug: permission-editor-scope-invalid
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • The permissions you picked were meant for a new conversation, or a saved rule didn't match your approve or deny choice. Nothing was sent or decided.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the SMTO page in your browser, then open the conversation you were working in. The page may still hold permissions you picked for a new chat, even though this conversation already exists.
  2. Select Permissions next to the message box, set Apply to to This conversation, choose the permissions you want, and select Apply. An existing conversation's permissions must be saved in its own editor; choices made for a new chat can't be moved onto it.
  3. Send your message again. If this appeared while answering an approval request, check it is still waiting, then select Approve once or Deny / stop task again. The first attempt was refused before anything ran, so repeating it after the fix won't do anything twice.

What success looks like

  • Your message is accepted and a new Task starts, or the approval request closes and the Task continues.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep resending the same message with the same permission choice; it will be refused the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Server rejected a permission request because a pending new-conversation permission policy was sent for an existing conversation, an unknown policy scope was requested, or a saved approval grant's deny/allow mode contradicted the approve/deny action.

What this means

  • A pending policy is applied to an existing conversation, an unsupported policy scope is requested, or a saved permission grant's deny/non-deny value contradicts the selected decision. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • A pending policy is applied to an existing conversation, an unsupported policy scope is requested, or a saved permission grant's deny/non-deny value contradicts the selected decision.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect policy scope and grant decision separately; do not move a new-chat default into existing conversation authority implicitly.

How to fix it

  • Omit conversation_permission_policy and conversation_policy when the request carries a conversation_id or request_id; save an existing chat's policy through its permission-policy endpoint under /api/agent/chats instead. On confirmations, send a grant whose policy.mode is deny only with action=deny (and never with approve), and request only the global or conversation capability scope.
  • Use the existing conversation’s permission editor for that conversation. Use pending policy only when creating a new chat, and save the policy that corresponds to the chosen action.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported owning editor/approval path accepts a scope-consistent policy decision.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
